arguments.sql:
WITH PortfolioValues AS (
    SELECT 
        p.portfolio_name,
        SUM(h.quantity * s.current_price) AS total_portfolio_value
    FROM portfolios p
    JOIN holdings h ON p.portfolio_id = h.portfolio_id
    JOIN securities s ON h.security_id = s.security_id
    GROUP BY p.portfolio_id
),
TechValues AS (
    SELECT 
        p.portfolio_name,
        SUM(h.quantity * s.current_price) AS tech_value
    FROM portfolios p
    JOIN holdings h ON p.portfolio_id = h.portfolio_id
    JOIN securities s ON h.security_id = s.security_id
    JOIN sectors sec ON s.sector_id = sec.sector_id
    WHERE sec.sector_name = 'Technology'
    GROUP BY p.portfolio_id
)
SELECT 
    pv.portfolio_name,
    COALESCE(tv.tech_value, 0) AS tech_value,
    pv.total_portfolio_value,
    (COALESCE(tv.tech_value, 0) / pv.total_portfolio_value) * 100 AS tech_percentage
FROM PortfolioValues pv
LEFT JOIN TechValues tv ON pv.portfolio_name = tv.portfolio_name;

arguments.explanation: I am calculating the diversification metrics for each portfolio by counting the number of distinct sectors associated with their holdings and the total number of holdings. I then filter for portfolios with more than 5 distinct sectors and calculate the diversification ratio (sector_count / total_holdings).
arguments.question: Find portfolios that have holdings in more than 5 different sectors and show their diversification metrics
arguments.sql:
SELECT 
    p.portfolio_name, 
    COUNT(DISTINCT s.sector_id) AS sector_count, 
    COUNT(h.holding_id) AS total_holdings,
    ROUND(CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT s.sector_id) AS REAL) / COUNT(h.holding_id), 3) AS diversification_ratio
FROM portfolios p
JOIN holdings h ON p.portfolio_id = h.portfolio_id
JOIN securities sec ON h.security_id = sec.security_id
JOIN sectors s ON sec.sector_id = s.sector_id
GROUP BY p.portfolio_id
HAVING sector_count > 5
ORDER BY diversification_ratio DESC;
